Ian Badiali won the Shipping A.A. 440 yards championship in 52.1 seconds, and Len Rolls won the Veterans A.C. 880 yards championship. Ted Smith won the London Transport 7 miles Walk Championship at Wembley in record time.
Ted Smith had an off day, but Eglington and Ferguson showed improved form. Charlie Speechley, our evergreen at sixty-five years of age, again showed he can still show the youngsters how.

Ted Smith recently won the London Transport 7 miles walking championship. Geoff Gregory, who decided a short time ago to turn to running, has now given up the idea and is training hard for walking again.

McMullen lead the field home from Gerry Warr and Ted Smith, and in the match against Surrey W.C. we won with 89 to 126 pts. We also held an 8 x 110 yds. relay, and with several non-sprinters competing we saw a close race with Bob Wolton once again beating Coxon over the final sprint.
Ted Smith took second place in the Business Houses 2 miles Track Walk on July 15th in 15 mins. 24 secs. George Oliver won the Civil Service 2 miles Track Championship on July 18th.
The handicap was won by Ted Smith, with 8minutes, 2nd was D. Logan, 17 minutes and 3rd none other than the Handicapper, Bill True off 11.30.
Unfortunately we lost two of our leading men who failed to please the judges and coupled with the fact that Ted Smith was recovering from the effects of flu' we did well to finish 3rd.
Ted Smith.

Eric's time was 56mins. 18s. with Ted Smith 2nd and George Beecham 3rd. Eric and George both started training under Frank Elson at the Duke of York's Headquarters and naturally were both anxious to get their names on the cup as the first holder.

Eric Hall walked an excellent race in the 2 miles to finish 2nd to R, Goodall in 15 mins. with Ted Smith 3rd in 15.18. George Beecham 8th and H.McGreechan 10th were our scorers in the 5 miles, George Oliver 10th in the 4 miles and R, Newson 6th and L.

Others showing sustained improvement are Eric Hall and Ted Smith and our team for the National 10 should be the best for a number of years. Congratulations to Eric Hall on once again winning the Civil Service 7 Miles Championship and George Checkley on his 2nd place in the Police 7 miles championship.

We had great hopes however, of a placing with Stan Vickers, and Eric Hall, Kent and Surrey Champions, Syd James 2nd in the Surrey, George Checkley 5th in the Middlesex and Bob McMullen back from Canada and showing something like his old form, together with George Beecham, young Terry Clark and Ted Smith.
Don Fotheringham walked well to finish inside the hour and work his way into the third handicap team accompanied by Stan Vickers, Eric Hall and Ted Smith.
Bob McMullen with a generous 5 minutes, took first prize, with Ron West 2nd and Ted Smith 3rd.

Ted Smith was not far behind with Len Demmon and Terry Clark moving up to complete the scoring four. At 3 miles the lads were holding their own and even at this stage it looked as though the team race was in the bag.
There was more trouble when we heard that Ted Smith was going all the way to Swindon and back on a special ticket which only cost 7/-, whereas as the rest of us paid a £1.

Ted Smith found the track a little hard going after the road and returned 59.15s. Trevor Luck, our only other competitor, walked very well to get inside 60 minutes and thus gain his 7 miles in the hour badge.
In the Invitation Mile, John Davies was 6th in 4mins. 12 secs. an excellent performance, and as stated previously Stan Vickers was 2nd and Ted Smith 4th in a two miles walk.
Percy Luxon gained a brace of thirds in the Long Jump and Triple Jump and Ted Smith was 3rd in the walk. In Essex Percy Porter retained his Hammer title with a record throw.
Eric Hall retained his title in 56.5.8 with George Williams 2nd and George Beecham 3rd. In the Middlesex event at Parliament Hill Ted Smith finished 3rd.

Our "A" Team consisting of Eric Hall, Ted Smith and George Checkley by a fine display of walking, won the event with a distance of 8miles, 869 yards, seven yards better than Woodford Green and our "B" Team were 5th with 8 miles 240 yards.
In the final race of 2 miles, Ted Smith was 2nd and Joe Coleman 6th making a grand total of 173 points and maintaining our lead of 4 points to win.

Other positions were Ted Smith 10th, Ray Switzer 18th, Harry Shields 21st Bob Readman 22nd, D. Russell 27th, Nick Milsum 28th, Wally Emery 29th and veteran Bert East 34th, totalling 11 of the 39 finishers.

Our return match with Surrey Walking Club at Tooting Bec was held on 14th August when a field of 41 turned out. We provided the first five men home with Eric Hall, Dave McMullen, Ted Smith, Ray Switzer and G.
On 27th June Stan Vickers won the Stock Exchange 2 miles Track Walking Championship in 14m. 28.2secs. On 3rd July Ted Smith won the Business Houses 2 miles Track Walking Championship.

With fine efforts from Eric Hall, Ted Smith, George Checkley and Bob Newson, the latter practically killing himself to take Stan over the last couple of laps, we won the team race from Woodford Green.
Ted Smith was our first man home in (10th) followed by McMullen, Checkley and Newson, 12th, 15th and 16th. We thus finished 2nd in the Scratch Race despite not having our 2 Olympic men.
Ted Smith,showing his true form,was 4th,Syd James 12th, Checkley 5th.McMullen 7th and Newson 13th.After this we can hope to regain the Berman Cup in our own Open on Nov24th.

Ted Smith was our great hope for the individual title and at two miles had a lead of afew yards over the field. From the three mile point however, he must have become very tired at the sight of Met vests for he found himself walking with six or seven of their men from then on.
Packing well, our lads put their team in the first twelve positions with Ted Smith 7th, Dave McMullen 8th, George Checkley 9th, Syd James 11th and Bob Newson 12th!

To those of you who are going on to the track I wish to thank you for your support during the winter and if you support Ted Smith in the same manner then we should have a bumper year.

Other Club finishers were Ted Smith(4th in 14.36.2) and Eric Hall(6th in 14.40.4). On the same day (July 13th) we sent a team to Birmingham to defend our team title in the Outer Circle 25 miles Walk,which we duly accomplished in no uncertain manner by scoring 16 pts. to Leicester W.C's 36 and Royal…
Ted Smith was only 7 sec. behind in 9th place and he too gains an Honours Badge. Ray Hall was unlucky to miss standard by only 19 sec. but we feel certain he will achieve it next year.
…Club, beating Highgate, Polytechnic and many other fancied clubs in the process. A particularly fine effort was that of Ted Smith in finishing fourth and George Checkley sixth.…

Complete with Ted Smith's speed oil, Eric Hall's soap and Jack Goswell's map of Kent, Yours Truly, OTTO VON VICKERS set out on May 3rd for East Berlin, with long-distance runner Jack Haslam and team manager Les Truelove, for the international 25 km. run and walk.

Stan and Eric were sadly missed in the 3000m. walk, although Ted Smith and John Knifton gleaned a valuable three points between them. Prior to the 3000m steeplechase Clive Shippen paid the penalty of insufficient warming-up by pulling a thigh muscle when negotiating a hurdle.
The ease with which both Bob Barnes and John Knifton covered seven miles was encouraging, - and in our winning 'A' team also , Ted Smith,always ready to give his all.
Since the Autumn he has trained from Belgrave Hall with Eric Hall, Ted Smith and John Knifton and attributes much of his recent good form to the help they have given him.
Our two Internationals Stan Vickers and Eric Hall, walked together to finish in 56:30, followed by John Knifton 58:27 and Ted Smith 58:54. Scoring six aside we beat M.P.A.A. by 24 pts, to 54.

We have had a fair amount of individual success; Eric Hall and Ray Middleton taking the first two places in the Civil Service '7'; Stan Vickers winning the Stock Exchange '7' and Ted Smith the Transport '7'.
The team was Ted Smith, Bob Barnes, George Checkley and Hugh McGrechan. Barnes emphasised once again his great potential and another of our younger walkers who gave promise for the future was P.

The only Belgrave medal-winner in this year's championships was Ted Smith whose 15:28.6 placed him 3rd in the two mile walk. Dave Carter performed well to finish 4th in the 220yds final, and Terry Newell and Dave Mitchell both qualified for the final of the 880yds; but nothing of note was produced.…

Ted Smith, Hugh McGreechan and Charlie Walker are the proud fathers of newly born sons, whilst John Keown and Eric Gebbett and Jumbo Masters are equally proud of their daughters---perhaps we'll have a ladies section yet !
Four of our leading walkers, Ray Hall, Ted Smith, Bob Barnes and Ray Middleton seen here together at the start of the 1960 Club 2 mile Championship.

Lapping the Common for the second time, the leading position was unaltered and interest turned to the handicap award. Bob Barnes was trying hard to catch John Knifton and was six places clear of Ted Smith 30th.
The police won the former and ourselves the latter. Ted Smith won the Monday race in 15:31 with H.

The Club 2 mile Track Championship was won by Bob Barnes (15:16.2) at Hurlingham on May 26th. Ted Smith (16:14) was second and John Keown (16:30.2) third. The same day a few lads travelled to Leicester for the "Mercury '20'".
The second handicap incorporated a match against M.P.A.A. which the Police won 33-45. Bob Barnes won the handicap from Don Bartliff and Ted Smith; Bob's time being 15:01.
Ray Middleton finished second in the '2' with Ted Smith 9th. Non-scorers from all clubs were allowed to take part in this race and first of those to finish was Gerry Cameron in 14th position.

Ted Smith was our first man home (8th) in 15:53, but with Surrey finishing 5 in 6 and the Police well represented we were a poor last. Charlie Maclennan (4:05) won the Club handicap from Fotheringham (2:35) and Smith (1:45).
